sources.title: Set goals with OKRs
sources.author: Google re:Work Editorial Team
sources.reliability: high for Google's described practice; not independent effectiveness evidence
sources.notes: Page explicitly says originally published 2016 and preserved as a historical record. No assumption that every detail is current company-wide policy.
sources.access_evidence: Retrieved introduction, setting objectives/key results and checklist warning.
supported_claims: OKRs pair objectives with measurable key results.
KRs should express outcomes rather than activities and include credible discoverable completion evidence.
OKRs are not intended as a master task checklist.

sources.title: PMI Lexicon of Project Management Terms, Version 5.0
sources.author: Project Management Institute
sources.reliability: high for PMI terminology; not comparative outcome evidence
sources.notes: Definition only; workflow details are not attributed to the lexicon.
sources.access_evidence: Official 36-page PDF retrieved; printed page 23, PDF page index 25, RACI definition inspected.
supported_claims: RACI is a type of responsibility assignment matrix using responsible, accountable, consulted and informed statuses for stakeholder involvement.

sources.title: Stakeholder Management and RACI: Who Does What, and Who Answers for It
sources.author: Project Management Institute
sources.reliability: high for PMI's published role guidance; blog is not a formal universal standard
sources.notes: Dated 29 July 2026. AI incidents discussed in article are outside adopted claim scope.
sources.access_evidence: Retrieved role definition table and section on accountable ownership.
supported_claims: Responsible performs work and may be multiple people.
Accountable is one owner of the outcome.
Consulted supplies input; Informed receives progress and decision information.

sources.title: What is MoSCoW Prioritization?
sources.author: Agile Business Consortium
sources.reliability: high for DSDM definitions and recommendations; not independent delivery guarantee evidence
sources.notes: Dated 28 May 2026. Contextual effort percentages are not implemented as mandatory thresholds.
sources.access_evidence: Retrieved four category rules, timeframe section, effort-balancing caveats and dependency tips.
supported_claims: Categories are Must, Should, Could and Won't Have this time.
Must concerns viable minimum; Should can have a workaround; Could has lower omission impact.
Priorities depend on timeframe and can differ across project/increment/timebox.
Must should not depend on a lower-priority requirement.
